svg.title: A client who wears a behind-the-ear hearing aid tells the nurse, 'It isn't working right and it keeps whistling at me.' Which actions should the nurse take? (Select all that apply.)
svg.desc: When a hearing aid is not working, the nurse first checks the simple causes: the BATTERY, the on/off switch and volume, and CERUMEN occluding the ear mold or canal. A loose or improperly seated ear mold is the usual cause of feedback whistling. NEVER IMMERSE A HEARING AID IN WATER OR ANY LIQUID; clean the mold with a dry cloth and store the aid in a dry, safe container with the battery compartment open.
